title: Security Review Checklist for Beginner Projects
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of security review checklist for beginner projects.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: A security review is a structured pass over a project to identify risks and verify controls. A beginner checklist can cover inputs, trust boundaries, authentication, authorization, secrets, privacy, errors, dependencies, configuration, and tests. A checklist is a starting point, not certification: it cannot prove a project secure or replace threat-specific expert review.
understand.whyItMatters: A repeatable review catches omissions before a project is shared or released.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
A security review is a structured pass over a project to identify risks and verify controls. A beginner checklist can cover inputs, trust boundaries, authentication, authorization, secrets, privacy, errors, dependencies, configuration, and tests. A checklist is a starting point, not certification: it cannot prove a project secure or replace threat-specific expert review.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.title: Check input handling
examples.explanation: Record whether untrusted inputs and validation have been reviewed.

examples.title: Check access rules
examples.explanation: A review should verify permission enforcement for protected resources.

examples.title: Check secrets
examples.explanation: Review source and logs for exposed credentials.

examples.title: Record unresolved risks
examples.explanation: Unresolved findings should be documented and assigned, not silently ignored.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Use a 10-item review checklist for a toy project. For every item, mark pass, needs work, or not applicable, and record evidence or follow-up for any failed item.
steps: Use a 10-item review checklist for a toy project. For every item, mark pass, needs work, or not applicable, and record evidence or follow-up for any failed item.
Identify the relevant assets, inputs, or permissions.
Choose a control and explain why it applies.
Check edge cases and failure behavior.
guidedTask.starterCode: // Use a small fictional example. Never paste real credentials or private data.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Perform a documented security review of a small project you designed. Cover all checklist categories, prioritize findings by risk, list fixes, and retest before declaring readiness.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Perform a documented security review of a small project you designed. Cover all checklist categories, prioritize findings by risk, list fixes, and retest before declaring readiness.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.

hints: Review the project from outside its assumptions.
Inspect inputs, boundaries, permissions, and data flow.
Search source and logs for accidental secrets.
Record evidence and unresolved issues; checklist completion is not a security guarantee.
